title: Design principles for a micro-farm
summary: Ergonomic spatial layout, bed orientation, windbreaks, water flow management, pathways, and making the most of every zone.

pages.title: Designing a sustainable and efficient micro-farm
pages.text:
The **design of a micro-farm** helps you produce better, tire yourself less, and build a farm that lasts over time.

This module shows you how to organize your farm according to your needs and your land.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Concevoir une micro-ferme durable et efficace

pages.title: Design principles for a micro-farm
pages.text: Learn how to structure your production area, organize your movements, take the climate into account, and choose the key features of a bio-intensive micro-farm.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les principes de design d’une micro-ferme

pages.title: The goals of good space organization
pages.text:
In a **bio-intensive market gardening system on living soil**, good space organization makes it possible to:

- **reduce physical effort** and optimize working time,
- **protect and improve the soil**,
- **ensure crop health**,
- **adapt to the climate** and to the available resources.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les objectifs d’une bonne organisation de l’espace

pages.title: The principles of an efficient layout
pages.text: A good design makes use of every corner of the farm: corners, borders, the backs of buildings, and the spaces under certain structures or near fences can host compost bins, storage areas, organic matter stockpiles, sheltered nurseries, medicinal plants, or useful hedges. When well used, these spaces free up the central areas for cultivation.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les principes d’une organisation efficace

pages.title: Reducing travel and making daily work easier
pages.text:
Good space organization lets you work faster and with less effort. The goal is to cut unnecessary movements and make everyday tasks easier.

A few principles to apply:

- **Place water, compost, and tools** right next to the growing beds.
- **Organize work areas** in a logical and compact way.
- **Plan clear pathways**, accessible on foot or with a wheelbarrow.
- **Create simple, visible storage spaces**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Réduire les déplacements et faciliter le quotidien

pages.title: Using the zoning technique
pages.text: Zoning is a simple, proven method for distributing your crops and equipment according to how often you pass by them each day.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Utiliser la technique du zoning

pages.title: Organizing the farm by usage zones
pages.text:
**Zoning** means placing each element of the farm according to how often it is used: **the more often it is used, the closer it is**.

Here is a typical layout:

- **Zone 0**: central area for management, storage, and rest.
- **Zone 1**: intensive growing beds requiring daily attention.
- **Zone 2**: long-cycle crops, fruit trees, green manures, compost area.
- **Zone 3**: storage of organic matter or expansion space.

In practice:

- Plots of 10 beds are grouped around zones 0 and 1 to limit travel.
- Compost bins and water reserves are accessible to several plots.
- Trees on permanent beds along the edges provide shade, protection, and production.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Organiser la ferme par zones d’usage

pages.title: Taking the climate into account in your layout
pages.text: Sun, wind, dust, and rain directly affect your harvests. Building these factors into the design from the start protects your crops over the long term.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Tenir compte du climat dans son organisation

pages.title: Orienting and protecting crops from the climate
pages.text:
Once the space is well organized, you need to think about the orientation and protection of crops against the climate:

1. **Orient the beds** according to the path of the sun (North–South or East–West depending on the crops).
2. **Protect sensitive areas** (nurseries, lettuces, etc.) with natural shade or shade nets.
3. **Shelter from wind and dust** with windbreak hedges or trees along the borders.
4. **Manage rainwater** with ditches, raised beds, or good drainage.
5. **Set up small shelters** for tools, seedlings, or seeds.

Thinking about these elements from the design stage ensures good crop growth and limits losses.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Orienter et protéger les cultures face au climat

pages.title: Key features of a micro-farm
pages.text: To run smoothly day to day, a micro-farm relies on a few simple but essential pieces of infrastructure.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les aménagements clés d’une micro-ferme

pages.title: Storage, tool shed, and water points
pages.text:
Once the space is organized and protected, you need to plan the essential structures for the micro-farm to function well:

- **Storage**: seeds and tools kept away from moisture. Harvests kept in the shade before sale or processing.
- **Tool shed**: large tools under a simple roof; small tools hung or stored so they stay within reach.
- **Accessible water points**: a main reserve complemented by small water points close to the crops.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Stockage, abri à outils et points d’eau

pages.title: Compost bins, fruit trees, and fencing
pages.text:
Complete your layout with three structuring elements:

- **Compost bin**: 1 compost bin for a small farm, 2 for a medium one, up to 4 for a large one. It is advisable to place compost bins slightly away from living areas and frequently used work areas to avoid problems with odors, insects, or foot traffic, while making sure they remain easily accessible from the growing areas.
- **Fruit trees**: one bed along the border before the crops and another at the end of the plot (spaced 1.5 m apart). They provide shade, fruit, and protection.
- **Fence**: sturdy, well placed, with an easily accessible gate.

Anticipating these elements avoids costly reorganizations and makes the system run more smoothly from the start.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Compostières, arbres fruitiers et clôture

pages.title: Examples of layout models
pages.text: Depending on the available area, the number of people, and the purpose of the site, several configurations are possible.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Exemples de modèles d’organisation

pages.title: Adapting the model to your goals and your land
pages.text:
There is no single right model: the layout of a farm depends on your **goals**, your **resources**, and your **land**.

Discover 4 concrete examples to adapt to your needs: a subsistence farm, a medium-sized farm, a large commercial farm, and a training farm.

What matters is to design a system that is coherent, functional, and scalable, adapted to your realities.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Adapter le modèle à ses objectifs et à son terrain

pages.title: Subsistence farm and medium-sized farm
pages.text:
**Subsistence farm**

- 1 plot (10 growing beds) and 1 compost bin.
- Fruit trees along the border.

**Medium-sized farm**

- 3 plots (10 beds each) and 2 compost bins.
- Shared water reserve for all plots.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Ferme de subsistance et ferme moyenne

pages.title: Large commercial farm and training farm
pages.text:
**Large commercial farm**

- 12 plots and 4 compost bins distributed across the site.
- Easy circulation for wheelbarrows and carts.

**Training farm**

- Production area (6 to 12 plots).
- Training area (shelter, teaching storage).
- 3 to 4 compost bins and a tree-planted area.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Grande ferme-entreprise et ferme-école

pages.title: Conclusion
pages.text: Let's recap the three pillars behind the success of a bio-intensive micro-farm design.

pages.title: The three pillars of good design
pages.text:
A good design is a coherent and practical system that simplifies your daily work:

- **Efficiency**: organize the space to reduce travel and keep tools, water, and compost always within reach.
- **Adaptation**: design while taking into account the climate, the available resources, and the constraints of the land.
- **Scalability**: think of a flexible design, able to grow or adjust over time.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les trois piliers d’un bon design
